Resident Evil Biohazard and Resident Evil Village are the best games in the series. I've already written a review of RE Biohazard, so let's talk about RE Village.

This game best depicts the “horror” genre; it is not oversaturated with jump scares, scary music, or darkness. Each character is unique, with their own story, and frightening in different ways. I would like to be like Miss Dimitrescu, walking around my huge luxurious castle in a long dress, wearing red lipstick and hunting men. Well, okay, let's skip this point.

The uniqueness of the game is that in addition to horror elements, it contains a plot with deep meaning. I haven't seen horror like this often. Basically, you go around killing creatures just to kill creatures. The plot does not touch the soul, but here at the end I shed a tear.

Of course, the game also has its downsides. For example, not all glass breaks, bullet marks don't always remain, but the game is so beautiful that I can close my eyes to it.

To conclude, Ethan Winters is the best father.

Resident Evil Village is easily one the best modern Resident Evil games released to date. It continues the story of RE7, a few years later.

The characters were amazing and very well done, with great voice acting, especially Lady Dimistrescu.

The level design was great. Very detailed and easy to navigate between areas and explore around.

The story was engaging. Things were revealed at a nice pace keeping you locked in, which makes you want to see it through to the end.

The DLC added a nice extra story which expanded on the main story a bit, while doing its own thing, which was great.

Absolutely recommended for everyone. For RE fans is a must play 10/10

If you liked RE 7 you'll like this one. The graphics, sound design, acting, setting, are all amazing. Gameplay is what you'd expect from an RE game where your character moves very slowly and turns even slower (use the quick turn button!). Plenty of surprises along the way and the game throws the player into many different settings so it's always interesting. Bear in mind that I finished the game in Standard difficulty in about 10 hours, and that was watching every cut scene, exploring for extra items, backtracking to collect the golden chests, etc. For a game that lasts 10 hours, make sure to buy it a sensible price.

The game is good, but this PC port is abysmal. Constant slowdowns even if you're running with a good rig, audio isn't in sync with the animations and really awful blur that pops in and out. It's a shame because everytime a cool moment happens like a boss or something with lots of detail, it's ruined by one or more of these things. I'd say get it for console or pirate it if you're interested. Definitely don't buy it until Capcom patch this. :|

Resident Evil Village is a masterpiece of a game. The atmosphere is beautiful, the story is rich and full of lore. Genuinely cannot recommend this game enough. As a person who is fairly new to the Resident Evil franchise, this game is by far my favorite. I've played a bit of RE7, but this was the first Resident Evil game I ever fully finished.

It has some jumpscares here and there, but they aren't terrifying. They are just small out of nowhere scares, and I enjoy that a lot. It kept me on edge the entire time when they would pop up. There is also some gore from time to time if you're afraid of that, but otherwise this game is amazing.

This is a MUST if you play through the Resident Evil franchise, do not miss out on this game. Again, I cannot recommend this game enough, 10/10. Will be playing again.

I had an enjoyable time with Resident Evil 8. I feel as though the jump from RE8 to RE7 was how RE4 jumped from RE 1-3 was; a more action horror focus rather than survival horror, but in the good way like RE4 did. Good action sequences while not completely diminishing the horror aspect of the series.

You can tell RE8 is very much inspired from RE4 when you contrast the similarities in locale (European Rural setting), Set Pieces (Castles, Village, Fortified Strongholds), collecting coins and treasure from the environment to sell to a mysterious merchant to upgrade gear etc. There were some aspects I liked with this such as the added cooking mechanic to upgrade Ethan's stats like Health or Blocking by encouraging you to explore the locations a little more.

My only noticeable criticism with the game was the extremely strong game start, with a meh midway, and then an adequate finale. It's obvious they used the start of the game for the marketing since it's the most interesting aspect of it (IMO), it has a very strong hook to lure you into the rest. But I enjoyed the game enough to not be completely dis-satisfied either. The game does eventually tie in the lore between RE7-RE8 and even into the greater Resident Evil universe.

It's definitely worth playing for any fan of Resident Evil.

Not as good as RE7, but still a really fun Resident Evil game, and a great game in general. It sort of fumbles the balance between action and horror by never fully committing to what it wants to be.

Decent game, fun combat and acceptable difficulty on the "standard" setting; it's semi-challenging but never hugely frustrating. Unfortunately the game overstays its welcome; by the time you're in the final area, it throws a lot of similar enemies at you, over and over: it's just tedious. By the last perhaps four hours I was just trying to power through to the end, honestly.

Still, it ticks most of the survival horror checkboxes while improving on combat in an appreciable way. Maybe just a little bit shorter on the next one.

The environments are breathtaking, from the chilling grandeur of Castle Dimitrescu to the grotesque depths of Heisenberg’s factory, each teeming with tension and eerie detail. The atmospheric sound design and stunning visuals immerse players in a world where every shadow feels alive. Gameplay strikes an excellent balance between exploration, resource management, and combat. The crafting system and weapons ensure players are prepared for relentless, terrifying enemies, while puzzles provide a satisfying change of pace though aren't very long and could be considered too easy and some sections make the boss fights feel underwhelming, the overall experience is incredibly polished. Resident Evil Village solidifies itself as one of the series’ finest entries In my opinion.

Resident Evil Village is the eighth title in the RE series, set in a cold and medieval environment. The game continues some time after the seventh title, going from swamp lands to chilling village. If you enjoyed RE7, it is highly likely you will enjoy RE8 as well.

The pacing is a bit different than the previous title, as the game will throw much more enemies at you due to your larger arsenal. Also, rather than relying on a smaller inventory, you instead have a large inventory that you sort your items in. Personally, I think this is a weird change because it puts less emphasis on thinking about what items you need to be carrying with you where you go.

However, this title amps up the action more than the previous title, so the change was necessary for the pacing of game play. Overall, resident evil is one of the best kinds of survival horror in the market, and this game is more of that good feeling.

It's also a lot more open than 7, allowing you to stop and admire the view. The RE engine is dropdead gorgeous as well, and on my rig it ran great at max settings. Would recommend playing if you want a decent action shooter or if you enjoyed 7's story.
